columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Operated by Bluesky Social PBC (US public benefit corporation); reference implementation of the open AT Protocol for distributed social networks.
Microblogging similar to X/Twitter, short posts with text, images, and video via bsky.social and apps; one account as a shared identity across the social internet.
AT Protocol is open source; multiple apps can plug into the same protocol for portable identities, follows, and content.
Users can subscribe to independent moderation services and personalized algorithmic feeds from different providers.

strengths.title: User-controlled identity and experience
strengths.detail: Account and social graph can move across apps on AT Protocol, not locked into a single company’s product.

strengths.title: Transparent, open-source stack
strengths.detail: Public code and protocol enable oversight and new apps (long-form, short-form, etc.) using Bluesky accounts.

strengths.title: Modular moderation and feeds
strengths.detail: Choose moderation services and feed algorithms to tailor what you see and how content is filtered.

strengths.title: Familiar microblogging UX
strengths.detail: Posts, replies, and quotes feel like X/Twitter, easier onboarding for migrants from legacy networks.

weaknesses.title: Smaller user base and network effects (for now)
weaknesses.detail: Early-stage vs major networks, creators who need reach may treat Bluesky as a secondary channel.

weaknesses.title: Complex concepts for mainstream users
weaknesses.detail: Decentralization, AT Protocol, and custom moderation/feeds are powerful but harder to explain than a single-app network.

weaknesses.title: Ecosystem fragmentation risk
weaknesses.detail: Multiple apps and moderation services can fragment experiences and norms across implementations.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Bluesky is decentralized microblogging network on the AT Protocol, portable identity, custom feeds, and modular moderation. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Bluesky is a decentralized microblogging social network built on the AT Protocol, designed as a public conversation platform where users control their experience, identities, and moderation across interoperable apps. Official site.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Bluesky side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Bluesky you can use Community & Messaging as a first-class product job. The job is hanging out, announcements, and live conversation, not packaging knowledge into something strangers can browse later.

Using Kahana with Bluesky

You can use both. Bluesky keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep live conversation on Bluesky. Pin a Kahana hub or Club link in a channel, discuss live there, and assign the next ebook, video, or course from Kahana so the syllabus is not buried in the thread.
